kids.name: Maddie
kids.notes: Mildly lactose intolerant. Picky but improving with age. Dislikes tomatoes and tomato-based sauces. Generally resistant to new foods. Says she dislikes salmon, but parents want to keep offering it.

kids.name: Hamish
kids.notes: Picky eater. Loves pasta. Likes rice with soy sauce. Generally resistant to new foods.

key_principles: Favor low-cleanup/one-pan (or one-pan-plus-one-pot) dinners on weeknights
Lean on 'build-your-own' formats (tacos, pizza, etc.) as a reliable way to introduce variety without a fight
Keep serving nutrition-forward meals (salmon, roast veg) even when not popular with the kids yet - look for kid-friendlier formats rather than dropping them
OK to hide vegetables in kid portions when it helps a dish land (e.g. blended into a sauce or mac and cheese)
Lunches and snacks should have real variety across the week, same as dinners - not a fixed rotation
Ensure avoid heavy rich foods as these give Genevieve indigestion.
Lunches and snacks are designed for adults rather than kids please
No strict repeat-avoidance rule - use judgment on spacing repeats rather than a fixed week count
Seasonal: household is in Australia - winter (Jun-Aug) prioritise hot dinners/lunches, summer (Dec-Feb) prioritise grilled food and salads

Maddie: mildly lactose intolerant (moderate dairy, lactose-free swaps where easy) and dislikes tomatoes/tomato sauce (offer a tomato-free option on build-your-own nights); states she dislikes salmon but keep gently offering it in kid-friendly formats
Hamish: avoid broccoli-forward dishes as the main event, salmon patties (crumbed 'fish finger' shape works better), roast veg stacks, and pie fillings — all previously flopped
Genevieve: prone to indigestion from rich/heavy food - go easy on cream, butter, deep-frying, and heavy cheese where possible
likes: Maddie: grilled/roast chicken, steamed broccoli, potato gems, chicken nuggets with ketchup, rump steak, flathead (fried, kid-style), plain rice

Hamish: plain/white rice, rice with soy sauce, pasta (plain, non-tomato), build-your-own tacos, chicken nuggets with ketchup, sausages with ketchup, flathead (fried, kid-style), egg and soy fried rice, basic mac and cheese, bacon, cous cous (sometimes)
dislikes: Maddie: tomatoes and tomato-based sauces, salmon (stated dislike, still offered), most new/unfamiliar foods
Hamish: broccoli (often picked at), salmon patties, roast vegetable stack, pie filling (ate pastry only), most new/unfamiliar foods

favourites.name: Soy-glazed baked chicken thighs, rice & steamed broccoli
favourites.authored_by: The Weeknight Realist & The Child Nutritionist

method: Whisk soy, honey, garlic and ginger; toss chicken to coat.

Serve chicken over rice with broccoli on the side.

dinner.name: Soy-glazed baked chicken thighs, rice & steamed broccoli
dinner.authored_by: The Weeknight Realist & The Child Nutritionist

ingredients.name: cornstarch
ingredients.display: 1 tbsp cornstarch mixed with 2 tbsp water

method: Preheat oven to 200°C (400°F).
Whisk soy sauce, honey, rice vinegar, garlic and ginger in a small saucepan; simmer 2-3 min.
Stir in the cornstarch slurry and simmer until glossy and slightly thickened, about 1 min.
Lay chicken thighs in a baking dish, spoon over half the sauce, and bake 20 min.
Brush on the remaining sauce and bake a further 10 min until sticky and cooked through.
Meanwhile cook the rice according to packet directions, steaming the broccoli for the last 5-6 min.
Serve chicken over rice with broccoli alongside — a splash of extra plain soy sauce on the side for Hamish's rice if he wants it saucier.

dinner.name: Build-your-own hard-shell tacos (Old El Paso), seasoned beef & toppings bar
dinner.authored_by: The Weeknight Realist & The Child Nutritionist

ingredients.name: taco shells (Old El Paso)
ingredients.display: 12 Old El Paso hard taco shells

ingredients.name: grated cheese
ingredients.display: 1 cup grated cheese (+ lactose-free block for Maddie)

ingredients.name: tomatoes
ingredients.display: 4 tomatoes, diced (topping — kept off Maddie's plate)

method: Brown beef mince in a large pan over medium-high heat, breaking it up, 6-8 min.
Stir in cumin, paprika, garlic powder and salt, then a splash of water; simmer 3-4 min until thickened.
Warm the taco shells according to packet directions.
Set out beef, lettuce, cheese, sour cream, avocado, diced tomato and cucumber separately.
Everyone builds their own — keep diced tomato and heavy cheese/sour cream light or off Maddie's plate, cucumber slices in its place.

dinner.name: One-pan sausage & rice bake, with a tomato & cucumber side salad

ingredients.name: tomatoes
ingredients.display: 6 tomatoes, sliced (side salad — kept off Maddie's plate)

method: Brown sausage meat in a large oven-proof pan, breaking it into small pieces, about 6 min; drain any excess fat.
Add onion and garlic, cook until soft, 3 min.
Stir in rice, then pour in stock and bring to a simmer.
Cover and cook 15-18 min until rice is tender and the liquid is absorbed, stirring in the peas for the last 5 min.
While the bake cooks, toss the sliced tomato and cucumber with a little olive oil and salt for a light side salad.
Serve as-is for the kids; pass the tomato-cucumber salad separately for the adults and Hamish — kept off Maddie's plate for the tomato, and light on any extra dairy for Genevieve.

dinner.name: Egg & soy fried rice with bacon
dinner.authored_by: The Flavor Explorer & The Weeknight Realist

ingredients.name: frozen peas and corn mix
ingredients.display: 1 cup frozen peas and corn mix

method: Heat oil in a large pan or wok over high heat; cook bacon until crisp, about 4 min.
Push bacon to one side, pour in the beaten egg and scramble until just set.
Add 4 cups cold cooked rice (day-old if possible), breaking up clumps, and stir-fry 3-4 min.
Add the peas and corn, soy sauce and spring onions; toss until heated through and everything is coated.
Serve as-is — a proven favourite for Hamish (rice with soy sauce, egg), easy to portion small for Maddie.

dinner.name: Oven-tray chicken nuggets, wedges & corn (with a side salad for the grown-ups)

ingredients.name: chicken nuggets or tenders
ingredients.display: 1 bag frozen chicken nuggets or tenders (~700g)

ingredients.name: corn kernels
ingredients.display: 2 cups corn kernels, fresh or tinned

method: Preheat oven to the temperature on the nugget/wedge packets (usually 200°C).
Spread nuggets and wedges across one large tray (or two if crowded), spray lightly with oil.
Bake according to packet directions, turning once, until golden and cooked through — usually 18-22 min.
Steam or microwave the corn for the last 5 min.
Toss a quick side salad for the adults while everything else bakes.
Serve straight from the tray — the lowest-effort dinner of the week.

dinner.name: Crumbed salmon 'fish fingers', oven-baked fries & peas
dinner.authored_by: The Family GP/Dietician & The Child Nutritionist

ingredients.name: salmon fillets
ingredients.display: 600g skinless salmon fillets, cut into finger-width strips

method: Preheat oven to 200°C (400°F) and line a tray.
Set up three shallow bowls: flour, beaten egg, and panko.
Coat each salmon strip in flour, then egg, then panko, pressing the crumbs on firmly.
Lay on the tray, spray lightly with oil, and bake 12-15 min, turning once, until golden and just cooked through.
Bake the fries on a separate tray alongside per packet directions, and steam or microwave the peas.
Serve with ketchup — same crumbed-and-fried approach that worked well before, oven fries in place of potato gems this week.

snack.name: Lactose-free yoghurt pouch (or fresh fruit if unavailable)

dinner.name: Roast chicken, roast potatoes, broccoli & a lighter gravy
dinner.authored_by: The Weeknight Realist & The Family GP/Dietician
method: Preheat oven to 200°C (400°F).
Pat the chicken dry, rub with oil, salt and pepper; stuff the cavity with garlic, lemon and thyme.
Place chicken in a large roasting tray, scatter potatoes around it tossed in oil, salt and pepper.
Roast 70-80 min until juices run clear and potatoes are golden, basting once halfway.
Rest chicken 10 min. Skim excess fat from the pan juices, whisk in flour over heat, then gradually add stock, simmering until thickened — go light on the flour/fat for a lighter gravy.
Steam broccoli and serve alongside.
